input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS crypto remediation for KServe and serving data plane images

## Description

This epic makes the KServe component images and the serving data plane images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. It delivers a complete module inventory of the affected images and the remediated images themselves, with all non-validated crypto removed from the request path.

## Scope

- Build a module inventory of all KServe component images and serving data plane images: every linked cryptographic library, its version, and its FIPS 140-3 validation status.
- Remediate each image that links non-validated crypto libraries so that cryptographic operations in the request path use validated modules (e.g., rebuilding against platform-provided validated crypto where applicable).
- Update image builds, base images, and dependency pinning as needed to eliminate non-validated crypto from the request path.
- Verify the remediated images function correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (inference request path works end to end with FIPS-mode cryptography).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The module inventory covers every KServe component image and serving data plane image, listing each linked crypto library and its FIPS validation status, and has been reviewed by the owning team.
- After remediation, no KServe component or serving data plane image links a non-validated crypto library in the request path.
- Remediated images are verified to run correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster: model serving via InferenceService works end to end (deployment reaches Ready, inference requests succeed).
- All remediated image builds complete successfully in the existing build pipeline after the crypto library changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules — this epic covers the KServe and serving data plane portion.

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results for every serving-stack image — and drives it through the mandatory security review board milestones to submission to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventories, build attestations, and FIPS-mode test results produced by the serving-stack image remediation work (KServe components, serving data plane, and Platform Operator).
- Assemble the evidence package in the format required by the security review board and the certification laboratory.
- Present the package at the defined review board milestones and incorporate feedback until the package is accepted for submission.
- Submit the accepted evidence package to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations, and test results for every serving-stack image in scope (KServe components, serving data plane, Platform Operator), with no gaps against the consolidated inventories.
- The evidence package passes the security review board review at the defined milestones and is accepted for submission.
- The evidence package is submitted to the external accredited certification laboratory.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification laboratory turnaround is historically six to nine months and the review board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They are schedule risks, not conditions this epic's deliverable produces.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions

## Description

This epic adds a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces non-validated cryptographic library usage, enforcing the FIPS remediation in the build pipeline.

## Scope

- Implement a CI check that inspects serving-stack image builds for non-validated crypto library usage (linked libraries and request-path usage).
- Wire the check into the serving-stack build pipelines (KServe components, serving data plane, Platform Operator) as a gating step — a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto fails.
- Calibrate the check against the validated-module inventory so remediated images pass without false failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gating CI check runs on every serving-stack build (KServe components, serving data plane, Platform Operator).
- The check fails a build that links a non-validated crypto library in the request path, demonstrated by a test case that intentionally reintroduces such a library.
- The check passes on the remediated serving-stack images — no false failures against the validated-module inventory.
- The check's verdict is visible in the build pipeline results (pass/fail status attributable to the FIPS gate).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

# Document FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, so customers (notably public-sector) can plan compliant deployments.

## Scope

- Author documentation stating the FIPS support posture of the serving stack: which images use validated crypto modules, what is certified versus remediated, and the status of the external certification effort.
- Author documentation of cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requirements and any deployment constraints for the serving stack in FIPS mode.
- Content outline:
  - FIPS support posture of the model serving stack
  - Cluster prerequisites (FIPS-enabled OpenShift, required configuration)
  - Deployment guidance for FIPS-mode serving (including raw deployment mode considerations for restricted environments)
  - Certification status and how to obtain compliance evidence

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled deployment.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented remediation and the assembled compliance evidence (statements match what was built and submitted).
- The documentation is reviewed for accuracy against the platform architecture context for the affected components.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded with inferred teams and acceptance criteria derived from the HLRs.
- **Inferred team ownership**: the architecture context (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`) assigns KServe to RHOAI Serving; the Platform Operator owning team is not stated anywhere in the strategy or context — E002 is assigned to "RHOAI Platform" as an assumption that should be verified at planning.

- **Docs priority note**: E005 carries P0 despite HLR-4 being P2 — this is the mandated docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter priority is Critical), not a priority inversion. It does not push priority onto its dependencies.

Not applicable. The external dependency (accredited lab certification) does not gate any engineering deliverable: remediation (E001/E002), CI enforcement (E004), and documentation (E005) all deliver value independent of lab timing. The only lab-gated outcome is the certification decision itself, which is outside the strategy's engineering scope; E003's controllable deliverable is the submitted evidence package.
